{"message": "All 10 tasks in the spannerlearning/seed0 development batch were solved with the third candidate.

Summary of revisions:
1. planning-001: BFS planner assuming single-spanner carrying. Returned valid-looking plans, but all 10 tasks still reported plan_length=0. The BFS was technically searching but the earlier misinterpretation (treating `carrying` as exclusive) led to BFS termination without a goal — and likely the candidates were rejected outright because the returned plan failed VAL semantics, not because the planner ran correctly.
2. planning-002: refactored with explicit state encoding; still treated carrying as exclusive, still failed with plan_length=0 across all 10 tasks.
3. planning-003: corrected the model so the man can carry multiple spanners simultaneously (PDDL `carrying` is not exclusive — the precondition only requires `carrying ?m ?s`, not that it be the only one). Result: 10/10 successes with plan lengths 10–13 actions each.

Key insight: the domain has no drop action and the man can only carry one spanner at a time *visually*, but the PDDL semantics allow multiple `carrying` facts to coexist, which is required to make these instances solvable (man picks up spanner3 at location1 and one of spanner1/spanner2 at location4 en route to the gate, then tightens all three nuts).

Remaining uncertainty: development batch only; held-out performance is unknown. The BFS state encoding is generic and should generalize to other spannerlearning instances with the same domain, but I have no evidence beyond this batch.", "summary": "All 10 spanner tasks solved"}
